doc.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: His son Michael's singing and recording with students
summary: His son chose engineering then singing; Hanna records students on his projects, including Jeb Patton and Stan Young.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: And I see your son has a thing out now, he’s a singer?

I’m very proud of him because you know when he was young I wanted him to play the piano, and he said dad, that’s not for me. He told me point blank that he was going to be an engineer. But he never stopped singing. So now, he came back to me and he says, “I want to sing.” I says okay. Come to find out he’s a good singer. He had developed on his own. Sometimes your kids have to go away and get their own thing.

You know, some people, they don’t let their kids go. But when he told me he wasn’t going to be a piano player I said hey, I’m not going to force you. And he had to live his own life, I can’t live his life for him. But his singing, he’s not operatic, and he doesn’t sound like Billy Eckstine, he has his own sound, and he’s just naturally musical I guess, from being around me and my musical situation. But he’s naturally musical. And when you hear the record you’ll know what I mean. And what I did was I took several of my students, one by one, and I infused them into the recording session so that I would have professionals and my son and the students as well.
That’s a great experience for them.

Yes it was. And one of the guitarists, he’s a wonderful guitarist, named Stan Young, a young fellow, he really is a young fellow, he’s 25, 26, something like that. And he was just, when he heard the record he couldn’t believe how good it sounded. But I’m still doing that and I’m planning to do more. We have one coming out on Jeb Patton. We plan to do another one, we’ve got one, I have a young saxophonist by the name of Keytayake Aomori. Now he’s the son of the young bass player that I have on this record now. We’re putting out another one on him. And I plan to do some things that won’t include me, just the students, or just the new people. But on these first four it’s been me with everybody else, and me with Michael. “Michael Hanna at Home With Friends.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
